subject: humanities
passage: Completed in the 120s CE, the dome of the Pantheon in Rome is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world. Its builders had no steel bars to strengthen the concrete, so they controlled the dome's weight in other ways. Near the base, where the structure carries the greatest load, the concrete contains heavy stone and the walls are several meters thick. Toward the top, the walls grow thinner, and the builders mixed in pumice, a light volcanic rock, so that the upper dome presses down far less on the structure below.
stem: Based on the text, why did the Pantheon's builders use pumice in the upper part of the dome?

choices.A: To reduce the weight that the top of the dome placed on the parts beneath it
choices.B: To make the upper walls of the dome thicker than the walls near its base
choices.C: To replace the steel bars that Roman builders usually placed in concrete
choices.D: To make the dome larger than any other concrete dome built in Rome at the time

explanation.why: The text says the builders "controlled the dome's weight" without steel. It then explains that they mixed in pumice, "a light volcanic rock, so that the upper dome presses down far less on the structure below." So the pumice was used to lighten the top of the dome and reduce the load on the lower parts.
explanation.A: Correct. The text states that pumice was used "so that the upper dome presses down far less on the structure below."
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says the walls grow thinner toward the top, not thicker.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the builders had no steel bars at all, so pumice could not be replacing a usual practice.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text notes the dome's record size but never says pumice was used to achieve it.

checks.note: Best fit on the text alone.
